extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners and their counsel involved in USPTO disciplinary/reciprocal-discipline proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 for imposing reciprocal discipline by the USPTO based on state disciplinary adjudications, including burdens, defenses, deadlines, and notice/publication obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of reciprocal discipline (Selling v. Radford)
rubrics_metrics.description: State disciplinary adjudication creates a federal-level presumption that imposition of reciprocal discipline by the USPTO is proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under Selling, the USPTO ordinarily will impose the same discipline the state imposed unless the respondent clearly and convincingly demonstrates one of the specified defenses. The Director is 'not sitting as a court of review to discover error' in the state proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) — Due process deprivation (factor i)
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner may avoid reciprocal discipline by showing the procedure elsewhere was so lacking in notice or opportunity to be heard as to constitute deprivation of due process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent must create a genuine issue of material fact on this point by clear and convincing evidence. Merely alleging procedural problems without clear-and-convincing proof is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) — Infirmity of proof (factor ii)
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner may avoid reciprocal discipline by showing there was such infirmity of proof establishing the conduct as to give rise to the clear conviction that the Office could not, consistently with its duty, accept as final the conclusion on that subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be shown by clear and convincing evidence that the state record's proof is so infirm that the USPTO cannot accept the conclusion. The burden is on the respondent; courts have required a high (narrow) standard to overcome the presumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) — Grave injustice (factor iii)
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner may avoid reciprocal discipline by showing the imposition of the same discipline by the Office would result in a grave injustice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A genuine issue of material fact as to grave injustice must be demonstrated by clear and convincing evidence. Generalized appeals to sympathy or minimization of conduct are insufficient if they do not address this specific factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) — Nonexistence of state/public discipline (factor iv)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any argument that the practitioner was not publicly censured, publicly reprimanded, placed on probation, disbarred, suspended or disciplinarily disqualified can preclude reciprocal discipline if proven.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent must raise a genuine issue of material fact by clear and convincing evidence that the state did not actually impose the disciplinary sanction relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden and standard of proof (respondent's burden)
rubrics_metrics.description: In reciprocal-discipline cases, it is the respondent attorney's burden to demonstrate, by clear and convincing evidence, that one of the Selling/§11.24(d) elements precludes reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal case law (e.g., In re Kramer, In re Friedman) supports that the respondent must prove by clear and convincing evidence a genuine issue of material fact as to one of the listed defenses; mere disagreement with the state finding is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of response (40-day deadline under § 11.24(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner has forty (40) days from the Notice and Order to file a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for extensions or waivers must meet the regulatory standard to be granted; untimely responses (absent an approved extension) mean there is no timely filed response for the Director to consider and support imposition of the discipline. The Director 'shall consider any timely filed response' and may impose reciprocal discipline thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's limited review role (not a court of review)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director's review in reciprocal-discipline matters is narrow; the Director is not conducting a full appellate reexamination of the state proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of the presumption in favor of enforcing state discipline, the Director accepts the state adjudication unless the respondent meets the high clear-and-convincing standard on one of the §11.24(d) defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy must be identical to state discipline (types of discipline)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall impose the identical public censure, public reprimand, probation, disbarment, suspension, or disciplinary disqualification unless a defense under §11.24(d) is established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will mirror the sanction imposed by the state (e.g., public reprimand), subject to the respondent overcoming the presumption with clear-and-convincing proof of a listed defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice obligations (Official Gazette and notifications)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the order and give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 to state disciplinary agencies, courts of admission, and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary decisions are available for public review at OED's FOIA Reading Room. The Order directs publication and inter-agency notification consistent with regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to judicial review (petition under 35 U.S.C. § 32)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review of the USPTO Director's final decision may be had by filing a petition in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia under 35 U.S.C. § 32 within thirty (30) days after the date of the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See E.D. Va. Local Civil Rule 83.5 for procedural particulars; timely filing is jurisdictionally important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive sufficiency of respondent's arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: To prevent reciprocal discipline, a respondent must specifically address the §11.24(d) factors rather than simply arguing the misconduct was unintentional, insignificant, or excusing circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final order rejected arguments that characterized the Florida discipline as an unintentional 'failure to respond to an innocuous request' because they did not address the §11.24(d) factors and thus failed to meet the respondent's burden by clear and convincing evidence.
